title: Stop the load when a partner file is empty

ticket.subject: Nightly load crashed on empty partner files: we need a guard
body: The 02:00 load crashed because two of the partner's CSV files arrived empty, and nobody noticed until the
dashboards were blank. Before we wire a guard into the scheduler, I need the script itself:
- it takes the folder to check as its first argument (PowerShell: a `param()`), and does not hard-code any file
- for every `.csv` file of that folder that is empty (0 bytes), it writes the file name on **stderr**, one per
- it exits with status **1** when at least one file is empty, **0** otherwise, so the scheduler can stop.
- In bash: start with `#!/usr/bin/env bash` and `set -euo pipefail`.
Then run it once on `incoming/` and keep the evidence for the incident note, in `logs/`:
- what it wrote on stderr, in `logs/check.err`;
- its exit status (just the number), in `logs/check.status`.
Datapass does not run your script: it reads it, and it reads the evidence your own run left.

acceptance.text: The script exists, takes the folder as an argument, reports on stderr and exits 1 on an empty file.

checks.fail: No script reads as asked yet.

acceptance.text: logs/check.status holds the exit status of your run on incoming/.

checks.fail: The recorded exit status is not what a guard should return on today's files.

acceptance.text: logs/check.err names the empty files, and only them.

hints: `[ -s "$file" ]` is true when a file exists and is not empty; `for file in "$1"/*.csv; do ... done` walks the CSV files of the folder given as first argument. In PowerShell, `Get-ChildItem $Folder -Filter *.csv | Where-Object Length -eq 0`.
`>&2` sends a line to stderr (PowerShell: `[Console]::Error.WriteLine($name)`). Keep a status variable and `exit "$status"` at the end, or `exit 1` as soon as you know.
Run it and capture both: `bash bin/check-incoming.sh incoming 2> logs/check.err; echo $? > logs/check.status`. `$?` is the exit status of the last command, so nothing may run in between.
In PowerShell, run the script in a new process so its stderr and exit code are its own: `pwsh -File bin/check-incoming.ps1 incoming 2> logs/check.err; $LASTEXITCODE | Set-Content logs/check.status`.
